summary: Wooden CCC lookout built 1939 near Sturgis; registers say removed in the 1950s, yet a 1963 item still lists the station. A radio tower stands on the summit now.

facts.design: Wooden tower about 30 to 40 feet high with a log-sided cabin

access.note: Reached by Vanocker Canyon Road; a road to the summit is used by hikers. Radio towers now stand on the summit.

visit.trail_note: No lookout left to climb; the summit guide calls the walk a short, but fun hike

facts.status_note: Lookout gone; a radio tower now stands on the summit.

events.note: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps
June 1940 newspaper item: secondary or emergency lookout, used only in times of fire hazard
August 1948 fire 25 miles south of Deadwood and Lead, discovered by emergency lookout Wesley Groshong; described as definitely man-caused
Byron Hazeltine listed as lookout personnel
July 14, 1954 fire near the lookout burned half an acre
April 1962 Lead Daily Call item: Royce Coffield stationed at the lookout
June 1963: Veterans Peak and Norris Peak stations to be manned depending on weather
Decade only: the register and summit guide say the 1950s, so 1950 is a placeholder year within that decade; the 1963 item conflicts

corrections.why: The register and the summit guide say the 1950s, and a June 1963 newspaper item still lists the station as manned. The record's 1950 is more exact than the sources support.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the summit guide say the 1950s; a June 1963 item still lists the station. The record's 1950 is left unchanged here and flagged in corrections for a human to decide.

notes_for_editor: Removal year conflicts: the register and summit guide say the 1950s; a June 1963 newspaper item (quoted on a lookout page, original not checked) still lists the station, so the record's 1950 is flagged in corrections. The access fact rests on the summit guide, which describes a road to the summit and says nothing about gates or closures; the summit is now a radio site, so check before a visit. Staffing names come from two lookout pages (firelookout.com and westlookouts), not from the original newspapers. Record elevation 1621.5 m matches the register's 1,622 m.
